response.sql: WITH dc AS (SELECT d.district_id, d.A3 AS region, COUNT(*) AS account_count FROM account a JOIN district d ON d.district_id = a.district_id GROUP BY d.district_id, d.A3), ra AS (SELECT district_id, region, account_count, AVG(account_count * 1.0) OVER (PARTITION BY region) AS region_avg FROM dc), ab AS (SELECT district_id, region, account_count, account_count - region_avg AS above_region_avg FROM ra WHERE account_count > region_avg) SELECT district_id, region, account_count, above_region_avg, account_count * 1.0 / AVG(account_count * 1.0) OVER () AS ratio_to_avg_above FROM ab ORDER BY ratio_to_avg_above DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: Districts on file means an inner join of account to district. Only districts with at least one account are counted, so a district with zero accounts is not in the region average.

The region is district.A3. The region average is the mean of the per-district account counts within that region. The final ratio divides by the mean count across all above-average districts, taken before the top-10 cut.
Ties at the 10th place are broken arbitrarily.
